deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes on 'topologie modérée' (tame topology). On the previous page Grothendieck defines equisingularity in a way that does not depend on the category of spaces chosen (topological, PL, algebraic, analytic). A diagram of spaces (X_j) indexed by a poset is equisingular along a locally closed Y ⊂ X_{i0} if, near each y ∈ Y, the part of the diagram over i0 is locally a product (Z_j × Y') → X_j by open embeddings, with Y' corresponding to {a} × Y'. In short, the whole diagram is locally trivial along Y.

This page specialises to an increasing filtration X_0 ⊂ X_1 ⊂ … ⊂ X by closed subspaces, with X = ∪X_i and X_{-1} = ∅.
- The filtration is called equisingular if, for every i, the diagram formed by (X_0 → X_1 → … → X) is equisingular along V_i = X_i − X_{i−1}. In modern terms: the strata are locally topologically trivial, compatibly with the whole flag.
- 'Feuilles (restreintes)' are the connected components of the V_i, i.e. connected strata. They partition X.

Proposition (frontier condition): if the filtration is equisingular, the closure of every leaf is a union of leaves.
- Proof sketch (not written on the page). Let F be a leaf in V_i and G a leaf in V_j, j < i, with y ∈ G ∩ F̄.
- In a product chart Z × Y' around y with Y' connected, F ∩ chart is a union of sets C × Y'. Its closure is C̄ × Y', which contains {a} × Y'.
- So G ∩ F̄ is open in G. It is also closed, hence G ⊂ F̄ because G is connected.

Parenthetical claim: if X is compact and the X_i are locally connected ('non-wicked' algebraic or analytic geometry), the closure is a finite union of leaves.

Further definitions and facts:
- The closures F̄ are the 'closed leaves'. F ↦ F̄ is a bijection between open ('restreintes'/'ouvertes') leaves and closed leaves, since F = F̄ ∩ V_i.
- Closed subsets that are unions of leaves are the same as unions of closed leaves. This class is stable under arbitrary intersections and finite unions.

The next page continues:
- inclusion of closures gives the incidence order on leaves;
- the boundary of F is F̄ − F;
- equisingularity is characterised as the frontier condition plus equisingularity of the diagram of X and all closed leaves along each leaf;
- this leads to a definition of an equisingular partition independent of any filtration.

Purpose: to set up an intrinsic, category-independent notion of stratified space ('dévissage' of tame spaces) for the tame-topology programme.
errors: The proof of the frontier condition is not written; it silently needs local connectedness of the strata, so that the chart parameter Y' can be taken connected. This hypothesis is only invoked later, for finiteness.

The finiteness claim (compact X, locally connected X_i ⇒ finite union of leaves) is not justified as stated. It needs some local finiteness of the number of components of the local models Z_k − Z_{k−1}, which local connectedness of the X_i alone does not obviously give. Grothendieck himself hedges ('pas méchante', '...').

Minor: the stability statement says 'toute intersection et toute réunion finie'. This is correct for closed unions of leaves (arbitrary intersections of closed saturated sets are closed and saturated), but saturation under arbitrary intersection should be noted as trivial while closedness under finite unions is what needs closedness.

ideas.what: Equisingular filtration: the whole flag of closed subspaces is locally a product along each difference stratum V_i
ideas.modern_name: Topologically locally trivial stratification (Whitney/Thom–Mather topological equisingularity; Siebenmann-type stratified sets without the cone condition)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney (1965), Thom (1969), Mather (1970), Siebenmann (1972); Zariski for equisingularity
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6 on tame topology and stratified structures, discusses such notions only programmatically

ideas.what: Leaves = connected components of strata; equisingularity implies the frontier condition (closure of a leaf is a union of leaves)
Bijection between open and closed leaves; closed saturated sets form a lattice stable under intersections and finite unions; incidence order on leaves (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Poset of strata / stratification as a map to a poset (Alexandrov topology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard; modern poset-stratified formalism: Lurie (Higher Algebra, App. A), Treumann, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka

ideas.what: Formulating equisingularity for diagrams of spaces indexed by a poset, in a way uniform across topological, PL, algebraic and analytic contexts
ideas.modern_name: Local triviality of poset-indexed diagrams / categorical axiomatics of stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: no single standard source; close in spirit to o-minimal / tame-topology frameworks (van den Dries) and poset-stratified spaces
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme states the wish for such a uniform framework

missed.claim: A 1974 manuscript definition of equisingularity as local triviality of a poset-indexed diagram of spaces, uniform across categories. Equisingular filtrations and partitions are defined from it, and the frontier condition and leaf poset are derived. This documents that the stratified-space foundations sketched in Esquisse (1984) were already being worked out in 1974.
missed.quote: On dit que la filtration est équisingulière si ∀ i ≥ 0, le diagramme formé de (X_0 → X_1 → … → X) est équisingulier le long de X_i − X_{i−1} = V_i
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it predates published remarks and is close to the modern poset-stratified viewpoint. The mathematics itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is standard stratification theory (local triviality implies the frontier condition, the leaf poset). The only mildly notable features are the diagram-theoretic, category-independent formulation and the 1974 date as a precursor of the Esquisse tame-topology programme.
